terms.meaning: Measures to fix unequal land ownership and help tenants and the landless.
A farm big enough to give a family a comfortable living after all costs.
Farmers pool their land, farm together and share the money after saving some for the land.
A contract that guarantees the landowner a fixed amount from the tenant for a fixed time.
Decentralised administration that lets local people take part and decide.

items.name: B. D. Jatti committee (1955)
items.formula: Proposed a ceiling of 116 acres of dry land or 27 acres of irrigated land per family.
items.example: Put in place in 1957, it mostly helped the rich.

items.name: Land Reforms Act of 1974
items.formula: Under Chief Minister D. Devaraj Urs: "The tiller became the owner of the land".
items.example: It ended all tenancy; claims went to a tribunal, appealable only in the High Court.

items.name: Land ceiling of 1974
items.formula: Dry land: 54 acres. Irrigated, one crop: 27 acres. Irrigated, two or more crops: 10 to 18 acres.
items.example: The Inam Abolition Act came in 1977.

items.name: Miller Commission (1918)
items.formula: India's first backward class commission, under Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV, led by Justice Lesley C. Miller.
items.example: The first reservation rule followed in 1921; Sahukar Chennaiah and M. Basavaiah led the non-Brahmin movement.

items.name: Havanur Commission (1975)
items.formula: Set up by Devaraj Urs under L. G. Havanur; used 1975 SSLC pass rates to measure backwardness.
items.example: Its 1977 government order empowered backward classes.

items.name: Later commissions
items.formula: T. Venkataswamy Commission (1983) and the Chinnappa Reddy committee under Ramakrishna Hegde.
items.example: Neither was implemented, due to political pressure.

items.name: Balwantrai Mehta committee (1955)
items.example: Karnataka passed the Mysore Village Panchayats and Local Boards Act in 1959.

items.name: Abdul Nazeer Sab
items.formula: Panchayat Raj Minister of the 1983 Janata government and architect of its changes.
items.example: It opened local government to dalits, backward classes and women.

mistakes.text: "The tiller is the owner" was the 1974 Act under Devaraj Urs, not the 1957 reforms.
The first backward class commission in India was Miller's (1918); Havanur's (1975) was Karnataka's first after independence.
More water means a smaller ceiling: 54 acres dry, but only 10 to 18 acres with two crops.
